newsitem.title: UK: Metals trade slowly on LME, copper remains adrift.
newsitem.headline: Metals trade slowly on LME, copper remains adrift.

text.p: Base metal markets began slowly on Tuesday, with little excitement seen during LME pre-market trading as prices mostly consolidated, traders said.

The copper market staged a mini-rally from overnight 7-1/2 month lows of $2,135 a tonne, trading between $2,140 and $2,151. But the bounce was beginning to attract selling, and recent trade at $2,147 was still $15 adrift of the Monday kerb close.
Traders said copper's bias remained to the downside, even though prices were oversold. Stocks increased by 4,075 tonnes, the market was in contango and funds were looking to sell, they said.
If support levels around $2,120 were breached, prices could well fall under $2,100, some said.
Zinc prices initially slid in thin trading to touch $1,475 on scattered liquidation before turning higher after a 5,175-tonne inventory fall.
Traders said talk of sizeable Chinese deliveries into the Singapore warehouse had yet to be translated into actual metal. The market settled at $1,487, still down $5 from Monday.
Aluminium was helped by a surprising 475-tonne stock decline, which halted the recent run of backwardation-induced increases.

Trade was in a narrow range, however, with the market $7 easier at $1,677. In the short term, the stocks trend remained unclear, and further inventory increases were likely given the widening backwardation.
Nickel prices were holding at an unchanged $6,670, with the market still unwinding after last week's heavy selling.
Tin was quiet, edging up $20 to $5,390, helped by a 120-tonne stock fall. Lead was looking vulnerable near $600, indicated at $601/603. Alloy was unmoved at $1,500/10.
